title: Untrusted Retrieved Content Crosses Trust Boundary

invariant.statement: Untrusted retrieved content must never cross from the data channel into the instruction channel of a model context. Retrieved data may be referenced as content but must not be parsed as agent instructions, tool calls, or policy.

claim.statement: If retrieved documents are concatenated into the system or developer prompt without role separation, an attacker who controls any document in the retrieval corpus can inject instructions that the agent will execute, including privileged tool calls and data exfiltration.

mitigation.summary: Tag retrieved content with an explicit data-channel role and surround it with a sandbox boundary the model recognizes. Strip or escape control sequences in retrieved text. Never concatenate retrieved strings directly into the system prompt; use a structured message with role=tool or role=user with clear delimiters.

references: OWASP LLM03: Training Data Poisoning (indirect via RAG corpus)
Greshake et al., Indirect Prompt Injection (2023)
